what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Some articles should be written for the reader's agent
sections.para: The reading list in a link went live 81 minutes after its brief, but it is written for people, and many readers now read through agents. A founder's agent used a threat tier article to refocus on organised crime. Content needs a second package for agents, with memory deltas, and rules for writing to someone else's agent safely.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Content needs a second package: a brief for agents
sections.para: Every entrepreneur now works with an agent, which can read more detail, check it against the project, challenge it and tell its person what matters. A founder's agent proved it. A pack for agents needs plain text, graph slices and critical reading rules. Deltas make it affordable, and writing to another's agent has rules.

sections.label: A founder, an article and an agent
sections.line: A founder's agent turned an article into a refocus
sections.para: A founder's agents were looping into ever more security work. Given Who are you protecting against?, with tiers T0 to T5, the agent saw the team was designing against states while backups were not done, and reset the target to T3, organised crime for money. It found a conclusion the writer could not, lacking the project context.

sections.label: Who reads what, now
sections.line: Messages now travel five routes between people and agents
sections.para: The routes: me to the person, me to their agent as a full brief, their agent to them as translation, me to my agent for packaging, and next, my agent to theirs through an encrypted lane. The uncomfortable conclusion: some articles should not go to a non-technical founder at all, only to their agent.

sections.label: Why an agent is a better reader for some things
sections.line: Agents read more, in context, and challenge it
sections.para: An agent takes more material and detail, reads it against code, backlog and decisions the writer lacks, and a good one does not simply accept it. Every new project already starts with a Claude session reading sgit.ai, the vaults, coding, nfrs, graphs and the newsroom: onboarding by reading, which others could be packaged.

sections.label: Memory: why this stays affordable, and why an agent would pay
sections.line: Agents would pay for deltas instead of rereading everything
sections.para: Articles are compression we control: a question on five articles cost 25,698 tokens by reading them against a median of 2,579 from the graph. Today a visiting agent starts from nothing each time. With an account, a key and its own vault, it could ask what changed. The agent pays not to pay.

sections.label: What a pack for someone's agent looks like
sections.line: A pack is a plain-text reading list for agents
sections.para: A pack is plain text, small enough to paste or attach. It says whom the agent serves, lists articles by number with markdown copies and graphs, gives the reasons each is included, sets rules for critical reading and keeping what was learned, offers a date to continue from, and a way back to the writer.

sections.label: Writing to someone else's agent, safely
sections.line: Packs for others' agents must avoid resembling prompt injection
sections.para: Text for someone else's agent can look like prompt injection, so packs have rules: they are data that never overrides the person, nothing hidden from the person, nothing asking the agent to send, buy, sign or share, disagreement explicitly invited, and nothing private, since a pack can be forwarded like an email.

sections.label: What to build next
sections.line: Next: agent packs, onboarding packs and a changes file
sections.para: Proposed builds: a For your agent button producing a plain-text pack for every reading list, onboarding packs for common starts, and articles/changes.json listing new articles, versions and corrections by date. The RiskMandate agent should choose person, agent or both per contact. Later come agent accounts and a direct encrypted line.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One story, one test, and nothing proposed is built
sections.para: The founder's story is a single case as told to me, a shape, not a measurement. The token figures come from five articles in The agent is the reader, and delta size is a design. The reading list is live; packs, onboarding packs, the changes file, agent accounts and the direct line are proposals.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: a voice memo, git logs and related articles
sections.para: Written by the site's agent from my voice memo of 11 October 2026, after the reading list went live. The founder is anonymous. Times come from the git logs of this site and the newsroom, token figures from The agent is the reader, and article numbers from the newsroom's articles/ids.json.
